tasks.question: A wellness program cohort shows 18% lower sick-day use than nonparticipants. Which explanation best accounts for the observed difference?

hypotheses.text: The program itself causally reduces sick-day use.
Self-selection into the program explains the apparent benefit.
The apparent difference is unstable sampling noise.

experiments.description: Randomly assign eligible employees to program invitation versus control and measure sick-day use with identical follow-up.

possible_outcomes.text: A similar benefit persists after randomization.
The benefit largely disappears after randomization.
Results vary widely with no stable direction.

observed.observation: The benefit largely disappears after randomization.

experiments.description: Match participants and nonparticipants on pre-program health and attendance, then re-estimate the difference.

possible_outcomes.text: A similar benefit persists after matching.
The benefit largely disappears after matching.
The estimate becomes erratic and directionally unstable.

observed.observation: The benefit largely disappears after matching.

experiments.description: Increase the observational sample without changing enrollment or adjustment procedures.

possible_outcomes.text: The original benefit remains statistically stable.
The estimate becomes directionally unstable.

observed.observation: The original benefit remains statistically stable.

controls.text: Verify baseline balance and adherence under the randomized assignment.
Use the same outcome definition and follow-up window in all groups.

risks.text: Selection bias from healthier or more motivated employees enrolling.
Outcome-coding drift between participant and comparison groups.

tasks.question: A new database engine appears 27% faster than the old engine in a benchmark where the new engine is always run second. What best explains the speedup?

hypotheses.text: The new engine has an intrinsic execution-speed advantage.
Warm operating-system and database caches from run order explain the apparent speedup.
The benchmark difference is dominated by random timing noise.

experiments.description: Randomize engine order and reset relevant caches between runs while keeping the workload identical.

possible_outcomes.text: The new engine stays about 27% faster.
The apparent speedup collapses after cache reset and order randomization.
Timings remain highly unstable across repetitions.

observed.observation: The apparent speedup collapses after cache reset and order randomization.

experiments.description: Run old-new and new-old back-to-back sequences on the same inputs and compare the second-run effect.

possible_outcomes.text: The new engine is faster regardless of position.
Whichever engine runs second gets most of the speed advantage.
No repeatable position effect appears.

observed.observation: Whichever engine runs second gets most of the speed advantage.

experiments.description: Repeat many trials while retaining the original old-then-new order and no cache reset.

possible_outcomes.text: The new engine remains stably faster.
The measured difference fluctuates around zero.

observed.observation: The new engine remains stably faster.

controls.text: Reset caches or explicitly measure cache state before each timed run.
Pin the workload, data snapshot, hardware, and configuration across engines.

risks.text: Cache warm-up and order effects contaminate latency measurements.
Background system load differs systematically between engine runs.

tasks.question: A classifier gains 9 accuracy points on a benchmark after training on a newly assembled web corpus. What most likely explains the gain?

hypotheses.text: The new training method genuinely improves out-of-distribution generalization.
Benchmark examples or near-duplicates leaked into the training corpus.
The apparent gain is mainly random-seed variance.

experiments.description: Evaluate both models on a newly collected test set created after training and excluded from all corpora.

possible_outcomes.text: A similar accuracy gain persists.
The gain mostly disappears on the fresh uncontaminated set.
The sign and size of the gain vary sharply across reruns.

observed.observation: The gain mostly disappears on the fresh uncontaminated set.

experiments.description: Run exact and semantic deduplication between the web corpus and the benchmark, then retrain after removing overlaps.

possible_outcomes.text: The gain persists after deduplication.
The gain collapses after overlapping items are removed.
Results remain inconsistent across seeds.

observed.observation: The gain collapses after overlapping items are removed.

experiments.description: Repeat training over many seeds but continue evaluating on the same original benchmark.

possible_outcomes.text: The gain remains stable.
The average gain shrinks toward zero with high variance.

observed.observation: The gain remains stable.

controls.text: Maintain auditable train/test provenance and deduplicate before training.
Use identical model capacity, optimization budget, and evaluation code.

risks.text: Train/test contamination or near-duplicate leakage inflates benchmark accuracy.
Hyperparameter tuning indirectly overfits the public benchmark.

tasks.question: After a factory ventilation change, one installed temperature sensor reports a persistent 2.5 C drop. What explanation best fits the effect?

hypotheses.text: The ventilation change truly lowered local air temperature by about 2.5 C.
The installed sensor drifted out of calibration around the intervention time.
Ordinary environmental variation produced the apparent drop.

experiments.description: Place a recently calibrated reference sensor beside the installed sensor before and after repeating the intervention.

possible_outcomes.text: Both sensors show the same intervention-linked drop.
Only the installed sensor shows the drop while the reference stays stable.
Both sensors fluctuate inconsistently without a repeatable pattern.

observed.observation: Only the installed sensor shows the drop while the reference stays stable.

experiments.description: Swap the installed sensor with a calibrated unit while holding location and ventilation settings fixed.

possible_outcomes.text: The measured drop stays tied to the location/intervention.
The anomalous offset follows the original sensor rather than the location.
Neither unit shows a stable pattern.

observed.observation: The anomalous offset follows the original sensor rather than the location.

experiments.description: Repeat the intervention several times using only the original installed sensor.

possible_outcomes.text: The same drop repeats.
The reported effect varies substantially across repetitions.

observed.observation: The same drop repeats.

controls.text: Use a traceably calibrated reference instrument at the same location and sampling times.
Hold sensor placement, logging interval, and ventilation schedule constant.

risks.text: Calibration drift can masquerade as a physical intervention effect.
Spatial temperature gradients can confound comparisons across locations.

tasks.question: A treatment study reports a 12-point overall response advantage, but the treatment arm contains many more low-risk patients. What best explains the overall advantage?

hypotheses.text: The treatment improves response broadly across patient subgroups.
Subgroup imbalance creates the apparent overall benefit.
A time trend unrelated to treatment creates the apparent benefit.

experiments.description: Estimate treatment effects within risk strata and reweight both arms to the same subgroup distribution.

possible_outcomes.text: A similar benefit remains within strata and after reweighting.
The overall benefit disappears after stratification and reweighting.
Effects change unpredictably across strata and time.

observed.observation: The overall benefit disappears after stratification and reweighting.

experiments.description: Run a new randomized replication with blocked assignment by baseline risk.

possible_outcomes.text: A similar treatment advantage remains.
The treatment and control outcomes become similar when subgroup balance is enforced.
Results remain directionally unstable.

observed.observation: The treatment and control outcomes become similar when subgroup balance is enforced.

experiments.description: Enroll a larger sample using the same imbalanced assignment mechanism and analyze only the aggregate response.

possible_outcomes.text: The aggregate treatment advantage remains.
The aggregate difference becomes unstable around zero.

observed.observation: The aggregate treatment advantage remains.

controls.text: Balance or stratify assignment by baseline risk before estimating the treatment effect.
Use the same endpoint timing and response definition across arms.

risks.text: Simpson's-paradox-style subgroup imbalance distorts the aggregate treatment effect.
Differential dropout can alter subgroup composition after assignment.

tasks.question: A software optimization is reported to cut request latency by 35%, but the post-change benchmark processed fewer and simpler requests. What best explains the result?

hypotheses.text: The code optimization intrinsically reduces latency for the same work.
The benchmark workload changed, creating an apparent performance gain.
Compiler or runtime noise explains the measured difference.

experiments.description: Benchmark old and new binaries on the exact same pinned request trace, data snapshot, and machine.

possible_outcomes.text: The new binary keeps a similar latency advantage.
The latency advantage largely disappears on the identical workload.
Results fluctuate strongly between repetitions.

observed.observation: The latency advantage largely disappears on the identical workload.

experiments.description: Compare pre- and post-change workload traces for request count, query mix, payload size, and cacheability.

possible_outcomes.text: Workload characteristics are effectively identical.
The post-change trace is materially lighter and explains most of the timing difference.
Trace differences are small and inconsistent.

observed.observation: The post-change trace is materially lighter and explains most of the timing difference.

experiments.description: Repeat the benchmark using the current lighter workload for both several times.

possible_outcomes.text: The new binary remains faster.
The measured difference oscillates around zero.

observed.observation: The new binary remains faster.

controls.text: Replay the identical pinned workload and data snapshot for both binaries.
Pin compiler/runtime settings and machine resource limits.

risks.text: Workload drift makes before/after latency incomparable.
Thermal or frequency scaling can bias sequential performance measurements.

tasks.question: A retrieval system jumps 14 points on a QA benchmark after indexing a new corpus. What best explains the improvement?

hypotheses.text: The retriever learned or exposes genuinely better semantic retrieval.
The new corpus contains benchmark-answer leakage or near-verbatim answer material.
Reranker stochasticity produced the apparent improvement.

experiments.description: Evaluate on a fresh QA set whose questions and answers were created after the corpus snapshot and are absent from it.

possible_outcomes.text: A similar retrieval gain persists.
The gain largely disappears on the fresh leakage-resistant set.
The gain varies strongly across repeated reranker runs.

observed.observation: The gain largely disappears on the fresh leakage-resistant set.

experiments.description: Search the indexed corpus for exact and semantic matches to benchmark questions and reference answers.

possible_outcomes.text: No meaningful benchmark overlap is found.
Many benchmark questions or answer-bearing passages are found in the indexed corpus.
Overlap findings are inconsistent across repeated searches.

observed.observation: Many benchmark questions or answer-bearing passages are found in the indexed corpus.

experiments.description: Repeat evaluation many times on the same benchmark and indexed corpus.

possible_outcomes.text: The gain remains stable.
The average gain collapses with high run-to-run variance.

observed.observation: The gain remains stable.

controls.text: Audit corpus provenance and exclude benchmark-derived or answer-bearing material before indexing.
Use the same retriever/reranker configuration and evaluation pipeline across corpora.

risks.text: Answer leakage makes retrieval quality look better without improved generalization.
Evaluation-query caching can contaminate repeated measurements.

tasks.question: A new learning algorithm beats a baseline by 4 points in one training run. Both methods are stochastic. What best explains the apparent improvement?

hypotheses.text: The new algorithm has a genuine average performance advantage.
The single-run difference is random-seed variance.
Unequal hyperparameter-search budget explains the apparent advantage.

experiments.description: Run paired evaluations across many shared random seeds with equal training and tuning budgets, then compare the mean difference and interval.

possible_outcomes.text: The new algorithm retains a positive mean gain with a clearly positive interval.
The mean difference shrinks near zero and the interval includes zero.
The new algorithm wins only when allowed a larger tuning search.

observed.observation: The mean difference shrinks near zero and the interval includes zero.

experiments.description: Repeat the original comparison over many seeds without changing either method's existing hyperparameter choices.

possible_outcomes.text: The new algorithm wins consistently.
The average advantage disappears as seed coverage grows.
The gap persists but is traceable to systematically better-tuned settings.

observed.observation: The average advantage disappears as seed coverage grows.

experiments.description: Run one additional seed while keeping the original tuning process unchanged.

possible_outcomes.text: The new algorithm wins again.
Either method may win; one extra seed is not decisive.
The result strongly tracks tuning-budget differences.

observed.observation: Either method may win; one extra seed is not decisive.

controls.text: Use paired/shared seed sets and report the distribution or confidence interval, not one run.
Equalize hyperparameter-search budget and stopping rules across algorithms.

risks.text: Random-seed variance is mistaken for a stable algorithmic improvement.
Researcher selection of favorable seeds or runs biases the reported result.
